answer.location_description: Small compact patch in the lower-right part of the field of view, about rows 15-17 and columns 19-22, well off the nodule centre (about 11 mm right of and 5 mm below it).
answer.shortcut_type: localized bright patch/marker off the nodule (artifact-like spot)
answer.mechanism: Hidden unit 9 (bias +88) has a tight block of large positive input weights in rows 15-17, columns 19-22. A bright spot there raises unit 9's activation. Unit 9 feeds layer-2 units whose net path to the output is positive. The main routes are u5 (-90 x -76), u7 (-49 x -92), u1 (-69 x -76) and u9 (-60 x -54), partly offset by u0 (+87 x -82) and u10 (-75 x 58). Summing w2 x w3 over all layer-2 units gives about +7.2k integer units for unit 9, so the patch pushes the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Unit 9 weights in the patch: r15 c20-22 = 81, 62, 47 (c16-19 = 79, 18, 80, 73); r16 c20-23 = 44, 78, 67, 71; r17 c19-22 = 79, 81, 71, 63. Nearly every value in this 3x4 block is strongly positive. The rest of unit 9's grid looks like mixed-sign noise (roughly uniform from -80 to 80), so a block this consistent is very unlikely by chance. Nothing about the nodule anatomy explains such a tight square detector far from the image centre. The rest of the network shows broader structure instead: centre blobs in units 18 and 20 and diffuse positive maps in units 8 and 27. Caveat: no other unit clearly duplicates the patch, and its logit effect (about 7k integer units through w2 x w3) is smaller than the main nodule unit 18 (about 30k). This is why confidence is only moderate.
answer.main_feature: Mainly central nodule density/size: units 18 and 20 have positive weight blobs over the image centre (rows ~10-17, cols ~6-17), and units 8 and 27 respond to broad bright tissue. All four route positively to the malignant logit, so larger, brighter central nodules score as more malignant.
